wiki.purpose: Provides the base structure for no-bake confections. The existing flavour of the cake contributes to the final product; chocolate or plain butter cake works best for rum balls and truffles.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Use within 2–3 days if made from fresh leftover cake.
wiki.notes: Cake crumbs are used as a base ingredient in confections such as rum balls, cake pops, and truffles. - **Source:** Can be made from leftover or slightly stale cake of any variety, or purchased as pre-made cake crumbs. - **Consistency:** Crumble or process cake into fine crumbs. Moisture content will vary depending on the cake type; adjust binding agents (rum, cream, condensed milk) accordingly. - **

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Derived entirely from the source cake recipe.

wiki.purpose: Provides deep chocolate flavour, dark colour, and bitterness without added sugar or fat. Used as a primary flavouring in cakes, biscuits, brownies, desserts, drinks, sauces, and dusting applications.
wiki.notes: Finely ground powder made from cocoa solids after cocoa butter is removed. Unsweetened and highly concentrated. Types and behaviour: - **Natural Cocoa Powder:** Light brown, acidic, sharp chocolate flavour. Reacts with baking soda for leavening; used in traditional cakes, brownies, and older recipes. - **Dutch-Processed Cocoa:** Treated with alkali to neutralise acidity; darker colour, smoother and milder flavour. Does not react with baking soda—use baking powder instead. Cocoa powder absorbs liquid aggressively; sift before use to prevent clumping. Blooming cocoa in hot liquid or fat enhances flavour depth and colour. Store airtight, away from heat and moisture to preserve aroma.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in dietary fibre; rich in magnesium and iron. Contains polyphenols and flavonoids with antioxidant properties. Naturally contains small amounts of caffeine and theobromine.

wiki.purpose: Thickens liquids into smooth custard; adds sweet vanilla flavour, creamy texture, and pale yellow colour. Acts as a convenient base for desserts and fillings.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place; keep airtight to prevent moisture absorption and clumping.
wiki.notes: Powdered mix, typically cornstarch-based, often flavoured with vanilla and coloured with turmeric or food-grade colour. Forms and - **Preparation:** Usually mixed with a small amount of milk to form a slurry, then stirred into the remaining hot milk while cooking to avoid lumps. - **Applications:** Used in custard desserts, trifles, fillings, and as a base for cream sauces in sweets.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Primarily a carbohydrate source; contains small amounts of iron and calcium depending on fortification. Nutritional impact per serving is modest due to small quantities used.

wiki.purpose: Provides sweetness, moisture, and glossy finish. Stabilizes sugar-based confections, prevents crystallization, and enhances texture in cakes, icings, desserts, and pastries.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a sealed container at room temperature; refrigerate if using perishable additives or flavourings.
wiki.notes: Common forms and Prevents crystallization in candies, icings, and caramel. - **Flavoured or Liqueur-Infused Syrups:** Can be lightly flavoured with vanilla, fruit extracts, or liqueurs to enhance desserts. - **Simple Syrup:** Typically a 1:1 sugar-to-water ratio; used to moisten cakes, sweeten beverages, or brush onto pastries. - **Usage Tips:** Adjust quantity to avoid excessive sweetness or moisture. Heat gently if incorporating into hot mixtures. - **

wiki.purpose: Creates a crisp, golden outer crust on crumbed meats and vegetables. Binds ingredients in stuffings, meatballs, and patties. Adds texture as a topping on gratins and baked dishes.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Keep dry breadcrumbs in an airtight container in the pantry for up to 3 months.
wiki.notes: Breadcrumbs are dried and finely ground bread used as coatings, binders, and toppings. - **Dry Breadcrumbs:** Fine texture; absorb moisture and create a thin, crisp coating. Standard for schnitzels, cutlets, and fried foods. - **Panko Breadcrumbs:** Japanese-style breadcrumbs; larger, flakier, and lighter. Creates a crunchier, airier coating than standard breadcrumbs. Preferred for bistro-style crumbed dishes. - **Fresh Breadcrumbs:** Made from day-old bread blended in a processor; soft and absorbs more moisture; used in stuffings, meatballs, and patties as a binder. - **Coating Technique:** Crumb using the standard sequence — flour → egg wash → breadcrumbs. Press crumbs firmly to adhere. Refrigerate 10–15 minutes before frying for better adhesion. - ** Panko keeps similarly.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Provides iron, B vitamins, and calcium; nutritional value varies slightly between brands and types.

wiki.purpose: Provides natural leavening and distinctive tangy flavour to sourdough breads and enriched doughs. Creates an open crumb structure and improved keeping quality through slow fermentation.
wiki.notes: A living culture of wild yeast and lactobacilli bacteria cultivated in a mixture of flour and water. Used as the sole leavening agent in sourdough bread, replacing commercial yeast with a slower, more complex fermentation. Requires regular feeding with fresh flour and water to maintain activity. Before use, the starter should be fully risen, bubbly, and smell pleasantly sour and yeasty — not sharp or acetone-like. A stiff sweet starter (lower hydration, fed with sugar) produces a milder flavour suitable for enriched doughs like cinnamon rolls. Can be stored in the refrigerator between bakes and revived with a few feedings. Discard a portion before each feed to maintain health and volume.

wiki.purpose: Adds sweet, delicate seafood flavour and firm texture to stir-fries, noodle dishes, curries, and grilled preparations. Cooks quickly and pairs well with bold sauces and aromatics.
wiki.notes: Shellfish with a sweet, delicate flavour and firm, slightly bouncy texture when cooked. Sold fresh or frozen, raw or cooked, shell-on or peeled. Green prawns are raw and turn pink-orange when cooked. For stir-fries and noodle dishes, peel and devein before cooking — the dark vein running along the back is the digestive tract. Cook quickly over high heat; they are done the moment they turn opaque and curl. Overcooking makes them rubbery. Store fresh prawns refrigerated and use within a day; frozen prawns can be thawed overnight in the refrigerator.

wiki.purpose: Adds concentrated tomato flavour, deep red colour, richness, and body to sauces, stews, and braises. Caramelises in hot oil to build a deep savoury base. Essential in Italian, Filipino, and many other cuisines.
wiki.storage: Store in the refrigerator after opening — tubes keep longest.
wiki.notes: A thick, concentrated paste made from tomatoes that have been cooked down and strained to remove seeds and skins. Deep red with an intense, slightly sweet tomato flavour. Used to add depth, richness, and colour to sauces, stews, braises, and soups. A small amount goes a long way. Fry briefly in oil at the start of cooking to caramelise the sugars and deepen the flavour before adding liquids. Sold in small cans, jars, or tubes. Can be frozen in tablespoon portions for convenience.

wiki.purpose: Adds sweetness, acidity, colour, and body to curries, sauces, soups, and stews. Provides texture, depth, and concentrated flavour depending on tomato variety and form used.
wiki.notes: Versatile tomato varieties for curries, sauces, stews, and general cooking. Choose the form based on recipe requirements and desired texture: * **Fresh Tomatoes:** Ripe and firm; ideal for salads, salsas, and fresh sauces. * **Roma:** Meaty, low in seeds; perfect for sauces, roasting, and cooking. * **Cherry / Grape Tomatoes:** Small, sweet, firm; great for roasting, salads, or quick sautés. * **Canned Tomatoes:** Peeled, diced, or crushed; excellent for long-simmered sauces and soups. * **Tomato Puree / Passata:** Smooth, liquid consistency; perfect for soups, sauces, and gravies where a silky texture is desired. * **Tomato Paste:** Concentrated tomato flavour; often caramelised slightly to deepen taste; use in small quantities for sauces, stews, and curries. For thicker consistency, drain excess liquid from canned tomatoes if needed. Store fresh tomatoes at room temperature (refrigerate only if very ripe). Canned, pureed, or paste forms should be stored in a cool, dry place and refrigerated after opening.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in vitamin C, vitamin A (from beta-carotene), potassium, folate, and antioxidants like lycopene. Supports immunity and heart health.

wiki.purpose: Provides mild, creamy flavour, excellent stretch, and golden browning when melted. Essential for pizza, lasagne, and baked pasta dishes where a smooth, even melt is desired.
wiki.notes: A mild, white Italian cheese with a soft, elastic texture and excellent melting properties. Available fresh (packed in whey or water) or as low-moisture block cheese. Fresh mozzarella is soft, moist, and delicate — best torn and used in salads or on pizza where it melts into creamy pools. Low-moisture mozzarella is firmer, grates easily, and gives the classic stretchy, golden melt on pizzas, lasagne, and baked pasta dishes. For lasagne, use low-moisture mozzarella for even melting and browning. Store fresh mozzarella in its liquid; block mozzarella wrapped in the refrigerator.

wiki.purpose: Adds intense umami, saltiness, and nutty depth to pasta, sauces, pesto, and baked dishes. Functions as both a cooking ingredient and a finishing cheese. A cornerstone of Italian cuisine.
wiki.notes: A hard, granular Italian cheese made from cow's milk, aged for 12-36 months. Intensely savoury, nutty, and slightly crystalline with a granular texture that melts into sauces. A little goes a long way due to its concentrated flavour. Grate fresh from the block for the best flavour and melting quality — pre-grated Parmesan contains anti-caking agents and loses its aromatic oils quickly. Use in pasta, risotto, pesto, sauces, and as a finishing cheese. The rind can be added to soups and stocks for extra depth. Store wrapped in wax paper or cheese paper in the refrigerator.

wiki.purpose: Adds sweetness, moisture, soft texture, and bright fruity flavor; works well in desserts, baking, sauces, preserves, and cooked fruit dishes.
wiki.notes: Used fresh, dried, or preserved. Canned apricots are most commonly sold as halves in syrup or juice and are soft and moist, making them suitable for baking, tarts, cakes, puddings, and compotes. Fresh apricots range from tart to sweet depending on ripeness and are ideal for eating raw, cooking, or preserving. Syrup-packed versions are sweeter and higher in sugar; juice-packed or drained options are lighter. Store fresh apricots refrigerated and use promptly; store unopened canned apricots in a cool, dry place and refrigerate after opening.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Good source of vitamin A, vitamin C, potassium, and antioxidants

wiki.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, moisture, and chewy texture to desserts, baked goods, energy bars, and confections. Can also function as a natural binder or sugar substitute in healthier recipes.

wiki.notes: Sweet dried fruit available whole, pitted, or chopped. Common varieties include Medjool (large, soft, very sweet) and Deglet Noor (smaller, firmer, subtly sweet). Forms and - **Chopped or Sliced:** Adds chewiness and natural sweetness to cakes, cookies, energy bars, and salads. - **Pureed:** Can be used as a natural sweetener or binding agent in desserts and baked goods.

wiki.notes: Distilled spirit made from fermented fruit juice, most commonly grapes. Adds warmth, aroma, and richness when used in cooking or baking. Often used in sauces, desserts, flambé dishes, and fruit macerations. Can enhance flavour in cakes, puddings, custards, and sauces. Use in moderation due to high alcohol content; alcohol mostly cooks off during heating but leaves concentrated flavour.

wiki.purpose: Adds roasted, slightly bitter, and aromatic coffee flavour. Enhances cakes, desserts, frostings, fillings, tiramisu, ice creams, beverages, and chocolate-based recipes.
wiki.notes: Derived from roasted coffee beans, available as whole beans, ground, or instant/soluble form. Coffee pairs exceptionally well with chocolate, caramel, cream, and spices like cinnamon and cardamom. Store airtight, away from heat, light, and moisture to preserve aroma and potency.

nutrition.calories: 2 per 100 g brewed (unsweetened); 0–50 per 100 g instant powder depending on added ingredients
nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains small amounts of potassium, magnesium, and niacin. Naturally contains caffeine; nutritional impact is minimal in typical culinary uses.

Spiced rum adds aromatic notes like vanilla, cinnamon, or cloves. - **

wiki.notes: Can also be added to coffee or cocktails. - **

wiki.purpose: Adds moisture, richness, and a tender crumb to baked goods. Provides structure and nutty flavour in gluten-free baking. Essential for friands, orange and poppy seed cake, and French patisserie.
wiki.storage: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the natural oils from going rancid.
wiki.notes: Finely ground blanched almonds with a soft, sandy texture and mild, sweet nutty flavour. Used in baking to add moisture, tenderness, and richness without the heaviness of wheat flour. Essential in friands, financiers, macarons, and many gluten-free baked goods. Can partially replace flour in cakes and pastries. Almond meal is not the same as almond flour — meal is coarser and made from whole almonds with skins, while flour is finely ground from blanched almonds. For best results in delicate baking, use blanched almond flour.

wiki.purpose: Provides dietary fibre, texture, and subtle nutty flavour; functions as a nutritional enhancer, textural component, or partial flour replacement in baked goods.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to prevent rancidity, especially for oat or rice bran which have higher fat content.
wiki.notes: Outer layers of cereal grains, typically wheat, oat, or rice, separated during milling. Adds coarse texture, nutty flavour, and substantial fibre to breads, muffins, cereals, and breakfast bars. Can be toasted lightly to enhance flavour. Absorbs liquid quickly, so recipes may require additional moisture when incorporated. Often used to boost dietary fibre and improve digestive health.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in iron, magnesium, phosphorus, and B vitamins; high fibre content supports digestive health

wiki.purpose: Enhances dough elasticity, rise, and final loaf texture; functions as a bread improver, dough conditioner, and volume enhancer in yeast-leavened baked goods.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place away from moisture and strong odours.
wiki.notes: Commercial additive used in bread and yeast doughs to improve texture, volume, and shelf life. Typically contains a blend of enzymes, ascorbic acid (vitamin C), gluten, and sometimes emulsifiers. Strengthens gluten structure, accelerates fermentation, and helps retain moisture, resulting in lighter, more uniform loaves with improved crust and crumb. Used in small quantities according to recipe instructions.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains small amounts of vitamin C and gluten; negligible contribution per typical recipe portion

wiki.purpose: Enhances gluten development, dough elasticity, and gas retention for better volume and texture in yeast breads. Improves chewiness and structure in whole grain or gluten-weak doughs. Essential for achieving soft, airy crumb in artisan breads, rolls, bagels, and pizza bases, and forms the base for plant-based meat substitutes like seitan.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in airtight container to prevent moisture absorption.
wiki.notes: Powdered form of wheat gluten with very high protein content (~70–80%). Commonly added to low-gluten flours (like whole wheat, rye, or spelt) to improve elasticity, structure, and rise in bread. Typically used at 1–3% of flour weight; too much can result in dense, chewy, or rubbery bread. Can also be used to make seitan (vegetarian protein) by hydrating and kneading into a meat-like texture. Mix thoroughly with flour to distribute evenly.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains small amounts of iron, magnesium, and selenium. Primarily contributes protein; low in fat and carbohydrates.

When using frozen, fold in gently to avoid colour bleed. Rich in natural sugars and moisture, they help keep baked goods soft and flavorful. Store fresh blueberries refrigerated and consume within a week; freeze for longer-term storage.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in vitamin C, vitamin K, and antioxidants; contains manganese

wiki.purpose: Adds bright, tart acidity and a distinctive floral-citrus aroma. Used as a finishing acid for Filipino dishes including pancit, bulalo, grilled meats, and dipping sauces. Balances rich, savoury, and salty flavours.
wiki.substitutes: can be substituted with a mix of lemon and lime juice, though the flavour will not be identical.
wiki.notes: Small, round citrus fruit native to the Philippines, about the size of a kumquat. Bright orange when ripe but typically used green. To use: cut in half and squeeze the juice over finished dishes, or serve as wedges alongside grilled meats, noodles, and soups. The juice Store fresh calamansi refrigerated for up to 2 weeks; bottled juice keeps refrigerated for months.

wiki.notes: Nectarines are firm, juicy stone fruits with smooth edible skin. - ** Can be poached, roasted, or grilled to intensify flavor. - **Pairings:** Complements berries, stone fruits, cream, custard, almonds, cinnamon, and honey. - ** Handle gently to avoid bruising. - **Substitutions:** Peaches can be used as a similar alternative with slightly fuzzier texture.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Good source of vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium, and antioxidants. Low in calories and fat while providing dietary fiber.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in vitamin C, vitamin A, and dietary fiber; provides antioxidants and natural sweetness.

Can also be roasted, poached, or grilled to intensify flavor. - **Pairings:** Complements cream, yogurt, nuts, spices like cinnamon or nutmeg, and other fruits. - ** Can be frozen or canned for longer storage. - **Substitutions:** Nectarine or apricot can be used as similar-tasting alternatives.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Good source of vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium, and antioxidants; low in calories.

wiki.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, acidity, moisture, tropical aroma, and vibrant flavor to both sweet and savory dishes.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store fresh pineapple in a cool place until cut; refrigerate cut fruit and consume within a few days.
wiki.notes: Pineapple is a tropical fruit with sweet, tart, and juicy flesh. - ** Drain syrup if using canned and not needed. Tidbits are small, uniform pieces ideal for baking, salads, or toppings. Can be chopped, juiced, or folded into batters. - **Pairings:** Complements coconut, cream, rum, brown sugar, ginger, and other tropical fruits. - ** Canned pineapple can be stored unopened at room temperature; refrigerate after opening. - **Substitutions:** Mango, papaya, or peaches can be used for similar tropical sweetness in some recipes.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in vitamin C, manganese, and bromelain enzymes; low in fat and calories.

Skin adds color and slight tartness. - **Pairings:** Complements cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, almonds, citrus, and other stone fruits. - ** Can be frozen or canned for long-term storage. - **Substitutions:** Peaches, nectarines, or apricots can be used for similar texture and sweetness.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Good source of vitamin C, vitamin K, potassium, and antioxidants; low in calories and fat.

Essential in Mediterranean cuisine, particularly Italian dishes such as pesto, tomato sauces, pasta, pizza, and caprese salads. Store refrigerated with stems in water or wrapped loosely in paper towel; basil is sensitive to cold and should not be stored for long periods.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Good source of vitamin K, vitamin C, folate, and antioxidants

wiki.notes: Coriander is a versatile herb and spice with distinct uses depending on form: - **Leaves (Cilantro / Fresh Coriander):** Add at the end of cooking or as a garnish to preserve bright, citrusy aroma. Ideal in curries, stews, salads, salsas, and chutneys. - **Seeds:** Toast lightly before grinding to unlock warm, nutty, and citrusy flavour. Used in spice blends, pickles, marinades, sauces, and curries. - **Ground / Powder:** Best used freshly ground for maximum aroma and flavour. Pairs well with cumin, turmeric, chili, and other spices in curry powders, rubs, and sauces.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in vitamin C, vitamin A, calcium, iron, and antioxidants; supports digestion, immunity, and adds aromatic compounds.

wiki.purpose: Adds earthy, slightly minty and floral aroma and flavour to dishes. Enhances savoury depth in sauces, soups, stews, roasts, and herb blends.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Fresh thyme can be refrigerated for up to a week; dried thyme should be kept in an airtight container in a cool, dark place for up to a year.
wiki.notes: Use fresh or dried leaves; remove woody stems before serving. Ideal in stocks, soups, stews, sauces, roasted meats, and vegetables. - **

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in vitamin C, vitamin A, iron, manganese, and antioxidants. Supports immune function, digestion, and adds trace minerals to dishes.

wiki.purpose: Adds sweetness, moisture, texture, and flavor; can be used for binding or topping in baking. Provides natural pectin for jams and jellies. Versatile for both sweet and savory applications.
wiki.storage: Store in the refrigerator crisper drawer for longest freshness.
wiki.notes: Can be used fresh, cooked, or pureed; varieties vary in sweetness and firmness; pairs well in baking, salads, sauces, and preserves. Tart varieties (Granny Smith) are best for baking and cooking as they hold their shape. Sweet varieties (Fuji, Gala, Pink Lady) are ideal for fresh eating and salads. Pink Lady and Granny Smith are Australian-bred varieties. To prevent browning, toss cut apples in lemon juice. Australian apple season is typically February to May.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Good source of vitamin C, potassium, and dietary fiber. Contains quercetin and other antioxidants, primarily in the skin.

wiki.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, moisture, flavour, and body; functions as a fruit component, natural sweetener, and partial fat or egg substitute in baking.
wiki.notes: Soft, sweet tropical fruit As bananas ripen, starches convert to sugars, increasing sweetness and aroma while softening the flesh. Ripe bananas are easily mashed and contribute significant moisture and natural binding to batters and doughs, making them ideal for banana bread, muffins, cakes, pancakes, and fritters. Sliced bananas are used fresh in desserts, tarts, and toppings, though they brown quickly when exposed to air; a light coating of lemon juice can reduce oxidation. Can be frozen whole or mashed for later baking use.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in potassium and vitamin B6; contains vitamin C and magnesium

wiki.purpose: Adds bulk, mild flavour, and texture to dishes. Provides crunch in raw preparations or softens for soups and stews. Enhances stir-fries, braises, salads, and Filipino dishes by balancing stronger flavours and acting as a versatile filler.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Keep in a cool, dry place or refrigerate in a perforated bag; lasts 1–2 weeks.
wiki.notes: Common forms and Shred, chop, or wedge depending on cooking method. - **Purple Cabbage:** Similar texture to green cabbage but with a slightly earthier flavour and vibrant colour. Excellent in salads, slaws, pickling, stir-fries, and braises. Colour may change with acidic ingredients. - **White Cabbage:** Mild-flavoured, firm leaves; excellent in stews, kimchi, slaws, and stir-fries. Holds shape well during cooking. - **Cooking Tips:** Cooks quickly; avoid overcooking to preserve colour, texture, and nutrients. Can be sautéed, boiled, steamed, fermented, or pickled. Outer leaves may be tougher—remove if desired. - **

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Excellent source of vitamin C and K; contains folate, calcium, and antioxidants; low-calorie, high-fibre vegetable

wiki.purpose: Adds natural sweetness, moisture, texture, and subtle earthy flavour; functions as a vegetable, dessert ingredient, and textural component in both sweet and savoury dishes.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, humid place or refrigerated to maintain freshness; remove tops to prolong shelf life.
wiki.notes: Root vegetable with sweet, earthy flavour and crisp texture. Can be grated, sliced, diced, or pureed depending on recipe. Provides natural sweetness and moisture, helping to tenderize baked goods. Can be roasted, steamed, boiled, or eaten raw.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Excellent source of vitamin A (beta-carotene), vitamin K, and potassium; contains antioxidants and fibre

wiki.purpose: Provides aromatic foundation, subtle bitterness, freshness, and light sweetness; adds body, depth, and texture to sauces, soups, stews, and vegetable-forward dishes.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, humid environment or refrigerate in a perforated bag; lasts 1–2 weeks.
wiki.notes: Crunchy, fibrous stalks used as a primary aromatic in mirepoix, soups, stews, and sauces. Dice finely for long-cooked dishes or slice larger for texture in stir-fries. Inner ribs are more tender and slightly sweeter, while outer ribs are stronger in flavour and higher in fibre. Leaves are edible and aromatic—ideal for garnishes, stocks, or flavour enhancement. Best when gently sweated or lightly sautéed to release natural sweetness.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in vitamin K, vitamin C, potassium, and folate; low-calorie, hydrating, and fibre-rich

wiki.purpose: Adds pungent, aromatic flavour and depth. Provides flexibility in intensity and texture depending on form: fresh for full-bodied aroma, paste for smooth blending, powder for convenience. Enhances sauces, soups, stews, curries, marinades, rubs, and roasted dishes; contributes both savoury complexity and subtle sweetness when caramelized.
wiki.notes: Common forms and Adds pungent aroma and depth of flavour. Can brown quickly and turn bitter if overcooked; add early for robust flavour or later for milder aroma. - **Garlic Paste / Minced Garlic Paste:** Smooth, concentrated form; blends easily into sauces, marinades, and curries. Use sparingly. - **Garlic Powder / Granulated Garlic:** Dried and finely ground; convenient for seasoning mixes, rubs, and baked dishes. Add during cooking or at the end depending on desired intensity. - **Storage & Tips:** Fresh garlic keeps best in a cool, dark, dry place. Paste and powder should be airtight to preserve aroma and potency.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in vitamin C, vitamin B6, manganese, selenium, and small amounts of calcium, copper, and potassium. Contains sulfur compounds that contribute to flavour and potential health benefits.

wiki.purpose: Adds a gentle, sweet onion flavour without the sharpness of regular onions. Functions as an aromatic base in soups and stews, or as a vegetable component in Filipino dishes like bulalo.
wiki.notes: A mild, sweet member of the onion family with a long white stalk that transitions to flat, dark green leaves. More delicate and less pungent than brown onions. The white and light green parts are tender and ideal for cooking; the dark green tops are tougher but excellent for stocks and broths. Must be thoroughly washed before use as soil gets trapped between the tightly packed layers — slice first, then rinse in a colander. Commonly sautéed as an aromatic base, braised as a side, or used in soups and stews. Store unwashed in the refrigerator for up to a week.

wiki.purpose: Adds umami, moisture, texture, and depth of flavor; versatile in sautés, sauces, soups, salads, roasting, grilling, and baking.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place, ideally in a paper bag in the refrigerator.
wiki.notes: Mushrooms are versatile fungi used fresh or cooked in a variety of dishes. - **Swiss Brown / Chestnut Mushrooms:** Firmer, slightly nuttier, holds shape well; ideal for sauces, roasting, or sautés. - **Button / White Mushrooms:** Mild flavor, versatile; good raw in salads or cooked in a wide range of dishes. - **Flat / Large / Portobello Mushrooms:** Meaty texture and earthy flavor; perfect for grilling, stuffing, or hearty recipes. - ** Cooking intensifies umami. Clean gently with a damp cloth; avoid soaking. - ** Use promptly for best texture and flavor. - **Substitutions:** Other edible mushrooms like shiitake, oyster, or cremini can be used depending on texture and flavor needs.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains B vitamins (B2, B3, B5), selenium, potassium, copper, and antioxidants. Low in calories and fat while providing protein and fiber.

wiki.purpose: Adds vibrant green colour, mild flavour, and nutritional value to dishes. Provides moisture and texture in pastries, quiches, soups, and sautés. Enhances overall presentation and complements other ingredients without overpowering.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store fresh spinach in a cool, dry place or refrigerated in a sealed bag.
wiki.notes: Common types and - **Leaf Spinach:** Larger, slightly stronger-flavoured leaves; suitable for sautéing, baking, or adding to sauces and soups. - **Usage Tips:** Can be used fresh or frozen. Squeeze out excess water before incorporating into pastries, pies, or quiches to prevent sogginess. Pair well with eggs, cheese, cream, or garlic for enhanced flavour. - ** Use frozen spinach directly from freezer; avoid repeated thawing to preserve nutrients and texture.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in vitamin A, vitamin C, vitamin K1, folate, iron, calcium, and antioxidants; low in sodium and sugar.

wiki.purpose: Provides mild, tender flesh that absorbs flavours well. Adds texture, moisture, and subtle sweetness to dishes.
wiki.notes: Best used young and firm for optimal texture. Can be eaten raw, grilled, baked, sautéed, or stuffed. Overcooking can cause excess moisture. Flowers are also edible. Store unwashed in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Good source of vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium, and antioxidants. Provides hydration due to high water content.

wiki.purpose: Mild, tender protein that absorbs sauces and seasonings readily. Ideal for elegant, restaurant-style dishes where delicate texture and clean flavour are desired.
wiki.notes: Veal is the meat of young cattle, with a mild, delicate flavour and tender texture. - **Veal Escalopes / Schnitzel:** Thin cuts, usually from the leg, pounded flat. Cooks very quickly — 1–2 minutes per side. Ideal for crumbing, pan-frying, or topping with sauces (Cordon Bleu, Scaloppine, Oscar, Madagascar). - **Veal Medallions / Steaks:** Thicker cuts used whole; excellent for bistro-style dishes with cream or wine sauces. - **Cooking Notes:** Veal has less fat than beef so it can dry out quickly. Cook over medium-high heat and keep residual sauce or butter present. Do not overcook — aim for just cooked through. - **Classic Bistro Pairings:** Lemon-butter, mushroom cream, Marsala, Cordon Bleu (ham and cheese filling), Oscar (crab/seafood topping).

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in B12, zinc, iron, and phosphorus; higher in protein and lower in fat than beef cuts.

wiki.purpose: Provides texture, nutty flavour, and dietary fibre; functions as a partial flour substitute, cereal grain ingredient, or textural component in breads, flatbreads, and salads.
wiki.storage: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place to preserve freshness.
wiki.notes: Whole wheat kernels that have been parboiled, dried, and cracked into smaller pieces. Quick-cooking and versatile, can be soaked, boiled, or added directly to breads, flatbreads, salads, and pilafs. Adds chewy texture, nutty flavour, and visual appeal. High in fibre and protein, it can be used to partially replace flour in bread or dough recipes, but may require additional hydration due to its water-absorbing properties.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Good source of manganese, magnesium, and B vitamins; high in dietary fibre

wiki.purpose: Adds texture, chewiness, and fibre to cereals, baked goods, and breakfast dishes. Acts as a binding agent in breads and cookies, and contributes mild, nutty flavour.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to prevent rancidity and maintain freshness.
wiki.notes: Rolled oats are flattened, lightly steamed whole oat groats. - **Usage:** Use in cookies, muesli, granola, oat breads, or porridge. Can be ground into oat flour for baking. Adds bulk, texture, and nutty flavour. - **Tips:** Toast lightly to enhance aroma or soak overnight for easier digestion. Adjust liquid when substituting for flour. - **

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains manganese, phosphorus, magnesium, copper, iron, zinc, folate, and B vitamins. Supports heart health, digestion, and sustained energy.

wiki.purpose: Provides deep, concentrated savoury flavour and body to pan sauces, gravies, and bistro-style accompaniments. Essential for authentic French-inspired restaurant sauces.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Commercial base keeps sealed in pantry; once opened, refrigerate.
wiki.notes: Demi glace is a rich, concentrated brown sauce that forms the base of many classic French and bistro-style sauces. - **Traditional Demi Glace:** Made by reducing equal parts espagnole sauce (brown sauce) and brown veal stock to a glossy, syrupy consistency. Intensely rich, deeply savoury, and complex. - **Commercial Demi Glace Base:** Available as powder or paste concentrate (brands like Major or Knorr Jus Lie). Dissolve per package instructions. Produces a consistent result suitable for high-volume or home cooking. - **Usage in Bistro Sauces:** Forms the backbone of many classic accompaniments — brandy mustard sauce, Madagascar green peppercorn sauce, Bordelaise, and Chasseur. Usually deglazed in the pan after cooking meat, then enriched with cream or butter. - **Substitutes:** A good quality beef stock reduced by 2/3 can approximate demi glace. Adding Worcestershire sauce and a small amount of butter improves depth. - ** Homemade demi glace freezes well in ice cube trays.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains sodium, potassium, and small amounts of iron from the concentrated meat stock.

wiki.purpose: Provides sweetness, umami, and a glossy finish to sauces, marinades, and stir-fries. Balances salty and savory elements, enhances caramelization, and softens strong flavors in Japanese and Asian dishes.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dark place.
wiki.notes: Mirin is a traditional Japanese sweet rice wine with low alcohol content. - ** Adds subtle sweetness and depth without overpowering other flavors. - **Pairings:** Complements soy sauce, sake, dashi, ginger, garlic, and sesame. - ** Once opened, refrigerate and use within a few months for best flavor. - **Substitutions:** Can be replaced with a mixture of sake and sugar or a mild rice vinegar with sugar if unavailable, though flavor will differ.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains trace amounts of minerals; primarily a source of sugars and minimal alcohol.

wiki.purpose: Provides heat, tang, and deep chili flavour; enhances complexity in sauces, marinades, stir-fries, and condiments.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a sealed container in the refrigerator to preserve freshness and colour.
wiki.notes: Sambal Oelek is a coarsely ground chili paste - **Usage:** Add directly to stir-fries, soups, sauces, marinades, or as a condiment. Adjust quantity according to desired heat level. - **Pairings:** Complements garlic, ginger, soy sauce, vinegar, lime, meats, seafood, and vegetables. - **

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains vitamin C, vitamin A, and small amounts of iron and potassium; primarily a source of spice and flavour.

wiki.purpose: Adds fiber, omega-3 fatty acids, protein, and nutty flavor. Enhances texture and nutritional profile in breads and baked goods.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dark place in an airtight container.
wiki.notes: Linseed, also known as flaxseed, can be used whole or ground. - ** Ground linseed can help bind ingredients and improve moisture retention in gluten-free baking. - **Pairings:** Works well with oats, nuts, seeds, honey, fruits, and other flours. - ** Ground linseed is best refrigerated to prevent rancidity. - **Substitutions:** Chia seeds, hemp seeds, or sesame seeds can be used for similar texture and nutritional benefits.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in omega-3 fatty acids, lignans, magnesium, phosphorus, and manganese.

wiki.purpose: Adds dietary fibre, improves dough structure and elasticity in gluten-free baking, and helps retain moisture for better texture.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption.
wiki.notes: Psyllium husk is a soluble fiber derived from the seeds of Plantago ovata. - ** Can also be used as a thickener for sauces or smoothies. - **Pairings:** Works well with gluten-free flours such as rice, almond, buckwheat, and oat flour. Complements seeds, nuts, and grains. - ** - **Tips:** Start with small quantities; too much can make dough gummy or overly dense.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in soluble fiber; negligible vitamins or minerals; supports digestive health and can aid in cholesterol management.

wiki.purpose: Enhances dough elasticity, structure, and gas retention. Acts as an emulsifier to stabilize mixtures containing fat and water, improving texture and consistency. Extends shelf life and promotes even browning and soft crumb development in baked goods, chocolate, spreads, and sauces.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry, airtight container away from light.
wiki.notes: Common usage and benefits: - **Emulsifier:** Helps blend water and fat-based ingredients in doughs, chocolate, confections, sauces, and dressings. - **Dough Conditioner:** Improves elasticity, gas retention, and crumb structure in yeast breads, rolls, and enriched doughs. - **Shelf Life:** Slows staling, moisture loss, and improves softness; promotes even browning in baked goods. - **5–2% of flour weight in bread recipes. Use sparingly, as excess may affect flavour or dough handling.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains choline (essential for liver and brain function), phosphatidylcholine, and phosphatidylinositol; naturally derived from soybeans. Minimal sugars and starch.

wiki.purpose: Adds crunch, flavour, healthy fats, protein, and nutrition to breads and baked goods. Enhances texture, visual appeal, and satiety.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place; refrigeration or freezing extends shelf life and prevents rancidity.
wiki.notes: Can be used raw, toasted, or incorporated into doughs and toppings. Adds texture and nutty flavour to breads, muffins, granola, and salads. - **

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in vitamin E, magnesium, selenium, and B vitamins. Contains healthy polyunsaturated fats, antioxidants, and plant sterols.

wiki.purpose: Provides structure, elasticity, and cohesion in gluten-free doughs and batters, allowing improved rise, crumb, and chewiness. Enhances moisture retention and prevents crumbling in baked goods. Also acts as a thickening and stabilizing agent in sauces, dressings, and gluten-free mixtures.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to prevent clumping.
wiki.notes: A polysaccharide derived from bacterial fermentation of sugars, Typically added at 0.5–1% of flour weight (about 1/4–1/2 teaspoon per cup of flour). Helps bind ingredients, trap gas during rising, and improve moisture retention. Can be used in breads, muffins, cakes, and sauces as a stabilizer or thickener. Overuse can create gummy or dense texture. Dissolve in water or oil before mixing into dry ingredients for best results.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Minimal micronutrients; mainly contributes soluble fiber, which can aid digestion and improve texture in recipes.

wiki.purpose: Adds vibrant red-orange color and a subtle earthy, peppery flavor to dishes. Commonly used in marinades, rubs, sauces, and traditional Latin American recipes.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dark place in an airtight container to preserve color and flavor.
wiki.substitutes: Can be substituted with paprika if unavailable, though the color will be slightly less vibrant.
wiki.notes: Can be rehydrated in warm water or oil before adding to recipes. Often used to color rice, stews, sauces, and marinades. Avoid exposure to moisture and direct sunlight, which can degrade both flavor and pigment.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains small amounts of iron and calcium

wiki.purpose: Adds warm, sweet, and slightly peppery flavour; versatile in both savoury dishes like stews, marinades, and sauces, and sweet dishes like cakes, cookies, and pies.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place for best aroma.
wiki.notes: Comes whole (berries) or ground. Whole berries are ideal for long-cooking dishes and can be removed before serving; ground is convenient for baking and spice blends. True allspice is not a blend, despite its name; flavour resembles a mix of cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains small amounts of manganese, iron, and calcium

wiki.purpose: Produces carbon dioxide to aerate and lighten baked goods; enables rapid and consistent rise without fermentation.
wiki.notes: A dry chemical leavening agent composed of sodium bicarbonate combined with one or more acid salts and a moisture-absorbing starch. Most modern baking powders are double-acting, meaning they release carbon dioxide gas once when moistened and again when heated, providing a more reliable and even rise. Used in cakes, biscuits, muffins, scones, and quick breads where yeast fermentation is not desired. Must be measured accurately; excess can cause bitterness or a coarse crumb. Loses potency over time and should be stored in a cool, dry place in an airtight container.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in sodium; no significant vitamins or minerals; used in small quantities

wiki.purpose: Adds background herbal depth and aromatic complexity; functions as a slow-release flavouring agent in long-cooked savoury dishes.
wiki.notes: Aromatic leaves from the bay laurel tree, used whole to gently infuse dishes during long cooking. Available fresh or dried, with dried bay leaves being more Added early in cooking to allow time for their subtle herbal, tea-like, and slightly woody notes to develop. Leaves remain tough and sharp even after cooking and must be removed before serving. Widely used in soups, stews, braises, sauces, rice dishes, curries, and stocks. Store dried bay leaves in an airtight container away from light to preserve aroma.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains vitamin A, vitamin C, iron, calcium, and manganese; used in small quantities so nutritional impact per serving is minimal

wiki.purpose: Produces carbon dioxide when combined with acid and moisture, aerating baked goods and giving them lightness and volume; functions as a chemical leavening agent in baking.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to maintain potency.
wiki.notes: A fine, white crystalline powder used as a chemical leavening agent. Requires an acidic ingredient (e.g., buttermilk, yogurt, lemon juice, vinegar) to activate and produce carbon dioxide gas, which helps doughs and batters rise. Overuse can result in a soapy or bitter taste. Can also be used for tenderising meat, neutralising acidic sauces, or as a cleaning agent in small household quantities.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in sodium; negligible nutritional value per serving as it is used in small quantities

wiki.purpose: Provides a convenient, balanced blend of warm spices for curries, sauces, and marinades. Adds colour, warmth, and savoury depth with a single ingredient.
wiki.storage: Store in an airtight container away from light and heat.
wiki.notes: A blended spice mix typically containing turmeric, coriander, cumin, fenugreek, and chilli. Yellow-gold in colour with a warm, earthy, mildly spicy flavour. Keen's is the most common Australian brand. Used as a convenient all-in-one spice blend for curries, sauces, soups, and marinades. Fry briefly in oil at the start of cooking to bloom the spices and develop deeper flavour. Different brands and blends vary in heat and complexity — adjust quantity to taste.

wiki.purpose: Adds sweet, aromatic, and licorice-like flavour to baked goods, spice blends, and savoury dishes. Enhances depth and aroma in breads, cookies, and pickled items.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight to preserve flavour.
wiki.notes: Fennel seeds are aromatic, slightly sweet, and licorice-flavoured. - **Forms:** Whole seeds or ground powder; lightly toast whole seeds to enhance aroma before adding to recipes. - ** - **Pairings:** Complements anise, caraway, cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom. Adds fragrance and subtle sweetness to both savoury and sweet baked goods. - **

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in iron, calcium, magnesium, and manganese. Provides small amounts of potassium and vitamin C. Used in small quantities, so nutritional impact per serving is minor.

wiki.purpose: Adds warm, sweet-spicy, and complex aromatic flavour to curries, sauces, stews, and marinades. Enhances depth, balances other spices, and provides signature Indian flavour profiles.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place.
wiki.notes: Garam Masala is a blend of aromatic spices - **Composition:** Typically includes cumin, coriander, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and black pepper. Variations exist by region or household. - **Usage:** Usually added towards the end of cooking to preserve aroma. Can also be used as a rub for meats or sprinkled over finished dishes for extra flavour. Best used in curries, stews, sauces, lentils, and vegetable dishes. - ** Ground blends lose potency over time; use within 6–12 months for optimal flavour. - **Tips:** Toast whole spices before grinding for deeper aroma. Avoid cooking at high heat for long periods as aroma diminishes.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in iron, manganese, magnesium, and small amounts of calcium, potassium, and vitamin C. Used in small quantities, so contribution per serving is minimal.

wiki.purpose: Adds a distinctively bitter, peppery, and slightly onion-like flavour as a topping or seasoning. Primarily used as a visual and aromatic garnish on flatbreads, naan, Turkish bread, and pastries. Lightly toasted seeds enhance flavour; used whole rather than ground in most applications.
wiki.storage: Store in an airtight container away from heat and light for up to 2–3 years.
wiki.notes: Small matte-black seeds with a slightly bitter, peppery flavour and subtle onion, oregano, and nutty notes. Popular in Middle Eastern, Indian, and North African cuisines; sprinkled on flatbreads, naan, pastries, pickles, vegetables, and legumes. In Filipino cooking, less traditional but useful for bread, rice dishes, and spice blends. Toast briefly in a dry pan to release flavour, but avoid burning.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains iron, calcium, potassium, magnesium, zinc, and antioxidants; traditionally valued for potential anti-inflammatory and digestive benefits

wiki.purpose: Enhances natural flavours, balances sweetness, strengthens gluten in doughs, and controls yeast activity. Coarse salts add crunch, texture, and visual appeal when used as a finishing touch.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place to prevent clumping.
wiki.notes: Salt is primarily sodium chloride and is essential for seasoning, baking, and preserving food. - ** Coarse salts such as sea salt or kosher salt provide texture and visual appeal; often used as finishing salts. - **Tips:** Adjust quantities according to type; coarse salts are less dense by volume than fine salts. - **Pairings:** Enhances the flavour of all foods, balances sweetness in baked goods, and improves texture in breads and pastries.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains primarily sodium; essential for fluid balance, nerve, and muscle function. Excess intake may impact blood pressure.

wiki.purpose: Adds nutty flavour, crunch, texture, and visual appeal. Can be incorporated into breads, pastries, cookies, granolas, and coatings; ground forms contribute to pastes, sauces, and dressings.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to preserve freshness.
wiki.notes: Common types and - **Black Sesame Seeds:** Earthier, slightly bitter; used for visual contrast, flavour, or in Asian desserts and breads. - **Usage Tips:** Toast lightly to release oils and enhance aroma. Can be added whole, crushed, or ground.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in calcium, magnesium, iron, phosphorus, and B vitamins. Contains healthy polyunsaturated and monounsaturated fats, plus antioxidants such as sesamol.

wiki.purpose: Ferments sugars to produce carbon dioxide and alcohol, causing dough to rise and developing flavor, structure, and aroma in baked goods.
wiki.storage: Store in a cool, dry place; refrigerate or freeze unopened yeast for extended shelf life.
wiki.notes: Available as active dry, instant (rapid-rise), and fresh yeast. Active dry should be bloomed in warm liquid (about 38–43°C). Instant yeast can be mixed directly into dry ingredients. Fresh yeast is highly perishable but offers strong fermentation. Sensitive to heat and salt; water that is too hot will kill it. Essential for breads, pizza dough, rolls, brioche, and fermented doughs.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Rich in B-vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B6, B9), selenium, chromium, and protein; contributes nutrients and umami flavor to baked goods.

wiki.purpose: Provides natural sweetness, moisture, and aromatic complexity; enhances browning, caramelisation, and flavor depth in both sweet and savory dishes.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed container.
wiki.notes: Honey is a natural sweetener produced by bees from floral nectar. - ** Retains moisture and promotes browning and caramelisation in baked goods. Raw honey preserves more enzymes and aroma; processed honey is milder and more consistent. May require reduced oven temperature and liquid adjustments in recipes. - **Pairings:** Complements fruits, nuts, yogurt, tea, cereals, cheese, and baked goods. - ** Crystallization is natural; gently warm to liquefy if desired. - **Substitutions:** Maple syrup, agave nectar, or golden syrup can be used with minor flavor differences.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains trace amounts of vitamin C, calcium, iron, magnesium, and antioxidants.

wiki.purpose: Adds sweetness, enhances yeast activity, improves dough texture, and contributes rich crust color and malt aroma in baked goods.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to maintain potency.
wiki.notes: Malt powder is derived from sprouted barley and comes in diastatic and non-diastatic forms. - ** Non-diastatic malt powder adds sweetness and malt flavor without affecting rising. Use in breads, rolls, bagels, and other baked goods. - **Pairings:** Complements flour, yeast, honey, chocolate, nuts, and milk. - ** - **Substitutions:** Honey or brown sugar can replace malt powder for sweetness, though enzymatic activity will not be the same.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: Contains small amounts of iron, calcium, and B vitamins. Primarily a source of carbohydrates.

wiki.purpose: Adds deep, robust sweetness, dark color, and moisture to baked goods and sauces. Enhances flavor complexity and richness, particularly in dense breads, spiced desserts, and savory glazes.
wiki.storage: Storage:** Store in a cool, dry place in a sealed container to prevent crystallization.
wiki.notes: Molasses is a by-product of sugar refining, dark, thick, and robust in flavor. - ** Blackstrap molasses is stronger and more bitter than light or dark molasses; adjust quantity to taste. - **Pairings:** Complements spices like ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, citrus, chocolate, and nuts. - ** Refrigeration can extend shelf life. - **Substitutions:** Light or dark molasses, honey, or brown sugar can replace molasses, though flavor intensity will differ.

nutrition.vitamins_minerals: High in iron, calcium, magnesium, and potassium. Blackstrap molasses contains more minerals than lighter varieties.
